author: Codex independent architecture design and direct critical-source review; no DeepSeek contribution to this card
status: paper design and legal prospective interface states only; no model, test, RTL, software, build, or board execution

main_result.candidate: prepare an entire source-return envelope before allowing its DMA to claim shared W order
main_result.new_action_relative_to_current_platform: A native noncommitting prepare request validates source READ and every destination WRITE range needed to consume that source AR. The DMA can receive this preparation without offering virtual AW to the four-DMA mux. Exactly one source stream without complete reserved return capacity receives a priming lease. Its corresponding first writable data then makes its first AW eligible. The lease covers the complete source AR, including all of its destination AW children, rather than only the first beat or first child.
main_result.why_this_constraint_is_real: Current mux pushes its W owner at the first downstream AW offer, even before AWREADY. The current TC obtains WRITE translation only after that virtual AW has entered its ordinary path. Small iDMA return FIFOs and independent AR admission can therefore couple address preparation, unreceived source data and immutable W order. This is an interface constraint, not a claim that two extra PTW ports or a DDR priority bit fixes it.
main_result.positive_capability: Page-limited source bursts longer than a DMA's return FIFO can stream without waiting for a future destination walk after they begin returning. Other prepared descriptors can wait without claiming W. A new DMA may start after the final true WLAST of the current envelope while its B is still outstanding, provided the old certificate remains pinned and its B accounting remains separate.
main_result.strong_control_result: Complete ordinary pretranslation + the existing first-R/AW coupler + one outstanding nonfullbuffer priming lease released at the envelope's last real physical WLAST has the same admission and retirement actions. Give it the same range records, ports and storage. It reproduces both decisive scenes; no exclusive scheduling or latency advantage follows from this card.
main_result.contribution_decision: Because that complete ordinary control is event-equivalent, priming order and first-data AW release cannot be presented as an independently new scheduling algorithm. If a concrete native paired record provides the full permission/return/W/B contract at strictly lower complete implementation cost than that control, the representation and interface organization can be a structure contribution. The present bit ledger does not establish that cost advantage. The useful positive result is a precise implementable capability and its narrow remaining cost gate, not a claimed performance win or proof of first publication.
main_result.one_next_question: Can one native paired preparation record safely bind all source-return bytes, WRITE children and their independent B lifetimes without duplicating context/queue state, and beat the fully implemented ordinary control in total state plus selection/control cost? Answer this bounded architecture-cost question before RTL performance trials.

exact_initial_contract.eligible: Normal nonoverlapping DDR copy; one active prepared envelope per DMA; four statically configured DID/PID pairs; aligned 64-bit words; source physical AR at most 256 beats and within one source 4 KiB page; all destination bytes within one completely WRITE-validated 4 KiB page. Destination AW may be divided into up to four known children. READ and WRITE permissions are independently requested and checked.
exact_initial_contract.scope_boundary: This restriction permits a 2 KiB source AR feeding two 1 KiB destination AW children. A source AR whose destination spans an unprepared next page is forbidden. Extending to two destination pages requires another PA/range/permission lease record and associated invalidation checks; it is not free. The ordinary min(source boundary, prepared destination extent) fragmenter gets exactly the same extent information.
exact_initial_contract.prepare_api: PAIR_PREPARE(src IOVA, dst IOVA, byte length, original DID/PID/privilege, job tag) uses a new native request path before the mux. It issues ordinary UNTRANSLATED_R and UNTRANSLATED_W checks through the existing translation service, one at a time. It does not send a fake virtual AW, issue physical AW, allocate W ownership, or synthesize a successful B. Special MSI/MRIF/debug/atomic/device cases are excluded and need the ordinary path.
exact_initial_contract.completion_api: The central record stores validated PA/range and captures success before granting the DMA. Actual AR/AW must match that record's flow, operation and precise IOVA coverage. A native TC prepared-record lookup can supply the saved result and genuinely avoid a new walk; merely setting an existing translated flag cannot be assumed to bypass all stages or permission checks. No new translation port or payload buffer is assumed.
state_steps: Accept one eligible descriptor into its prepared-record slot; acquire source READ and destination WRITE results. On a prepare fault, issue no physical source AR or AW and report the real fault through a defined job-error path.

Select a fully prepared slot with round-robin fairness. Before any nonfullbuffer source AR offer, allocate its global priming lease. Already offered AXI VALID remains stable. Enable from a quiescent state; no old unaccounted nonfullbuffer read may exist.

Allow that source AR. Other source streams must either reserve their complete return capacity in their private buffer or wait. Preparing other slots is allowed, but it must not create another unreserved payload return stream.

After corresponding first writable data has entered the existing byte FIFOs, allow this slot's first virtual AW offer. The initial aligned contract makes first R sufficient; general unaligned operation would need the complete first write-mask condition, not a generic first-R pulse.

Continue the remaining destination children from the same full validated WRITE coverage. Keep the source-return lease until all envelope bytes have crossed the actual physical W interface and the final child's true WLAST has retired. One child's WLAST or a virtual upstream WLAST is not this boundary.

Release the priming/write-order lease at final physical W retirement. Preserve source authorization until its physical R completion and destination authorization until every issued physical child B has settled and no later child remains. Cache replacement and a single B must not erase the paired range.

Invalidation has two states: unused prepared records may be discarded, while a launched record must either drain under its valid lease before invalidation acknowledgement or use an explicit supported abort/recovery protocol. Ordinary cache attributes are not permission immutability. Software cannot reuse/free the mapping before the appropriate invalidation completion.
exact_initial_contract.progress_assumptions: The downstream memory eventually serves accepted owner reads and accepts its legal writes; AXI alone does not give a finite cycle bound. Prepared records neither wait for subsequent software nor acquire a second potentially stalled translation after launching payload. A global lease is a finite nonpreemptive envelope, not permanent priority for one DMA.
exact_initial_contract.platform_limit: The current nonblock DMA0/1 use 512-beat full-job buffers, while other DMA instances use 3 beats. Small-buffer scenes therefore cannot be asserted as the cause of the old A8 board PN residual. Changing that supported configuration is an architectural experiment, not evidence that the present board kernel is deadlocked.

two_decisive_scenes.type: prospective legal interface sequence; not a new executed experiment
two_decisive_scenes.resources: One DMA with three 64-bit return-FIFO positions, one long accepted source AR, a cold destination WRITE mapping, and a shared R stage whose already asserted payload RVALID cannot be withdrawn. Count every intermediary return position as S; use a source burst longer than S plus the private three positions. If the fabric can absorb the whole burst, this scene does not apply.
two_decisive_scenes.ordinary_local_coupler_sequence: Source READ is translated and AR is accepted. Its first R is buffered, so the existing coupler releases virtual AW; only now does the ordinary TC request destination WRITE translation. The memory can keep serving payload before that new PTE exists. When aggregate return storage fills, one offered payload R is held. DMA cannot drain W until WRITE permission/PA returns; the required PTE R cannot pass the held common R stage. Fixed PTW priority cannot preempt an already held VALID, and could not prioritize a WRITE walk that had not yet been requested.
two_decisive_scenes.candidate_action: Complete WRITE preparation before the physical source AR. The future payload-to-W drain requires no new destination PTE for any byte in the envelope. The first-data AW release can open that drain using its retained PA. This removes this particular circular dependency under the stated memory-service assumptions.
two_decisive_scenes.strong_control: Full ordinary READ/WRITE pretranslation plus the existing coupler also removes this scene. It is a required capability, not candidate-exclusive benefit.
two_decisive_scenes.falsification: An actual path showing enough independent return storage for the whole source burst, PTE delivery independent of the held stage, or fully resident source data invalidates this circular-wait construction. A guard that forbids the initial source AR also prevents it, but pays its real fragmentation/admission cost.

two_decisive_scenes.type: prospective legal cross-ID interleaving state; not a current board trace
two_decisive_scenes.resources: Two three-beat FIFOs; both source READ and target WRITE are already valid; both long source ARs are accepted while no AW is offered. Each DMA uses its local first-R/AW coupler. The common return stage may switch between IDs at beat boundaries but must preserve an offered held beat.
two_decisive_scenes.sequence: Accept A AR then V AR before either returns. Accept A first R; A offers AW and becomes mux W owner. Accept and write A's first word. Return V's first three words before A's next word; V offers AW behind A, and its FIFO becomes full. Offer V's fourth R and hold it because V cannot write ahead of A. A needs more source R to finish its current W burst, but those responses cannot pass the held V beat. All actual AW/W order remains legal; no previously asserted VALID is withdrawn or reordered.
two_decisive_scenes.candidate_action: While W is empty, reserve A's nonfullbuffer priming lease before AR, so V's nonfullbuffer AR is not offered. A's data stream can drain its prepared writes. Later V can start at the final real WLAST, without waiting for A's B.
two_decisive_scenes.strong_control: Ordinary complete pretranslation + existing coupler + one outstanding nonfullbuffer priming lease with the same last-physical-WLAST release makes exactly the same decision. Current AW-based bank ownership alone cannot recall the two ARs accepted before the first AW; if an existing earlier gate prohibits them, this scene is unreachable there.
two_decisive_scenes.falsification: A mandatory whole-burst return policy that never interleaves in this way, sufficient full return reservation for V, or an earlier one-stream admission rule prevents this constructed cycle. This scene has no required pending PTE; it distinguishes source/W ownership correctness from a claimed PTE bottleneck.

complete_controls.exact_limit: It may prevent PTE queuing delay before payload selection but cannot change no-ID W ownership or retract a held payload R. C1 introduces the destination walk after the read has started; C2 is a payload ownership cycle even with all translations ready.

It can be correct with the same 3-beat buffer by limiting copy units to at most fully reservable source data. A 256-beat source requires at least ceil(256/3)=86 source units at this exact reservation limit, or a much larger buffer. This count is not a unique candidate gain because the complete streaming control below also uses one long AR.

complete_controls.control: ordinary backpressure and current AW-based bank owner guard
complete_controls.exact_limit: Backpressure preserves the blocked state; the guard is effective once AW ownership exists, and it respects selected VALID. It cannot cancel an old read accepted before ownership. Full-buffer admission exceptions must use a real capacity reservation, not a descriptor-size guess.

complete_controls.control: ordinary complete pretranslation + local coupler + one nonfullbuffer priming lease
complete_controls.implementation: Use the same per-flow prepared PA/range records and existing byte FIFOs. An arbiter holds one 2-bit priming owner before its source AR offer; block other unreserved reads, while full-reservation reads remain legal. Open AW with the existing local first-data coupler, retain the lease across every destination child covered by that AR, and release it at the last actual physical WLAST. Keep permission records and child-B accounting separately until all relevant responses complete. Existing banked_ctl already demonstrates WLAST-based ownership retirement; waiting for B is not needed for the W-order lease.
complete_controls.same_information_and_budget: All source/destination endpoints, validated extent, exact byte correspondence, real capacity reservations and child retirement events are equally available. No extra ports or payload storage are given to the proposal. This control matches C1, C2 and B-tail overlap; measuring those scenes cannot establish independent scheduling value.

complete_controls.control: min(source boundary, prepared destination extent) source fragmentation
complete_controls.exact_limit: With only the current destination segment prepared, it correctly limits AR to that extent. With the full one-page WRITE range and its child accounting prepared, it can also issue the same 2 KiB AR feeding two 1 KiB AWs. Giving candidate full-page coverage and control only one-child coverage would be an unfair information/state comparison.

state_and_interface_ledger.basis: Four eligible fixed DID/PID flows; PAddrWidth=56 in ariane_soc_pkg.sv:127; one prepared envelope per flow; up to four destination children; source payload buffer stays 3 beats per DMA. This is a concrete register proposal, not synthesized area and not a demonstrated cost reduction.

per_flow_added_bits.field: source and destination returned translation range
number of WRITE children issued and outstanding
fault cause and fault READ/WRITE selector
retained source IOVA, destination IOVA and prefix byte length for matching

global_added_bits.field: envelope real bytes remaining at physical W
one outstanding prepare owner, READ/WRITE operation, valid

state_and_interface_ledger.reuse_lower_bound: If actual existing descriptor storage can be pinned, addressed and reused through certificate/B retirement without losing FIFO capacity or adding equivalent shadow state, the 140-bit matching tuple per flow may be reused. That gives 687 proposed new bits. This reuse is not established by the current source: the ordinary job FIFO and read/write headers have their own pop lifetimes. Charge 1247 until a concrete reuse proof exists.
state_and_interface_ledger.selectors_and_critical_logic: Four fixed-DID decodes; original PID/privilege/type checks; source/destination IOVA/extent comparisons; prepared-result PA/range mux; 64-bit W strobe byte count into a 12-bit remaining counter; exact final-child-WLAST and per-flow B routing. Existing TC/spill/FIFO header storage remains counted in both designs. The independent prepare path needs arbitration into the existing translation service and a true prepared-result completion path; no new AXI ID is assumed.
state_and_interface_ledger.unclosed_costs: The ledger is not total implementation cost. Invalidation command integration, generation-wrap quiescence, pending-command state, job-error notification routing, sideband spill/queue state if native matching is replaced by a reference, timing cuts and arbitrary DID/PID support require exact designs. A 16-bit generation is not sufficient by itself: wrap must stop preparation and wait until all old records and inflight uses retire before reuse. S/G-stage context updates must invalidate the record as well as leaf cache entries. All these costs apply to proposal and ordinary control, and can erase any supposed structure advantage.
state_and_interface_ledger.no_free_fields: Existing request/response registers and inactive stage bits are not assumed to become free storage. Permission r/w bits may be reduced to operation-specific validation only under the fixed immutable per-record operation and lifecycle contract; it cannot authorize a different flow merely because PA is equal.

direct_source_evidence.fact: AW lock/first offer pushes W owner before a possible stalled handshake; W follows FIFO owner and pops on true LAST handshake.
Four-DMA mux, MaxWTrans8; DMA0/1 conditional512-beat buffer and others3; RAW_COUPLING_AVAIL0; fixed DID10+i/PID20+i.
An existing first-R/AW release mechanism stores AW headers and grants them after a real first-R handshake. It is an explicit strong baseline component, not new.
Coupler is optional and wires actual R first/handshake to AW. Current production disables it.
Masked byte-FIFO readiness controls R; actual byte presence determines writable data. First R is not universally the complete first write mask under arbitrary alignment.
Accepted descriptor has source/destination/length, then passes through an ordinary job FIFO and backend; no paired noncommitting permission API presently exists.

TC queues AW/AR, has limited W buffering, starts ordinary WRITE translation from AW before ordinary READ, captures response with unconditional response-ready, and supplies saved translated PA to physical completion channels.
Current guard is tied to immutable bank selection and AW/unfilled W ownership, not a complete per-job source-return preparation envelope; its write-order ownership retires at WLAST rather than B.
PTW/other DS clients share one AR arbitration and R spill/demux. This does not make DS and DMA private payload buffers one credit pool.
Request binds IOVA/DID/PID/type/privilege/bank. Response includes PA/range/error and independent r/w/x permission-related fields; a prepared operation must preserve those semantics.
Fault cause is12 bits, charged in the proposed failure state.

Board residual does not prove full PTW root cause. Prior real-model DSpriority changes demonstrate reachability under one return policy; small-buffer source/target mismatch and full owner-aware ordinary controls already exist.
Separate read/PTE ports, adaptive priority and longest feasible burst components already have strong precedents; DDR model priority is not equivalent to configurable MIG priority.
Committed source obligations are counted in real bytes; ordinary exact owner-aware drain already achieved its lower bound in existing runs.

primary_nearest_sources.title: Arm AMBA LTI Protocol Specification, ARM IHI0089 IssueE, 20 March2026
primary_nearest_sources.actual_read_scope: B1.1/B1.2 text web490–556; B1.3 text580–608; B4.1 ordering text1063–1092; B6.2 text1963–2011. Other chapters not fully reviewed.
primary_nearest_sources.finding: LTI already permits translation before transaction ordering and a lookaside data path. Its completion rules explicitly allow one translation for multiple compatible transactions in a validated region and require retention until all uses complete. Therefore early preparation, physical bypass and translation reuse are existing components. These passages do not specify this particular cross-DMA finite-buffer priming/envelope contract; absence from the passages is not a novelty proof.

primary_nearest_sources.title: Benz et al., A High-Performance, Energy-Efficient Modular DMA Engine Architecture, IEEE TC2024, DOI10.1109/TC.2023.3329930
primary_nearest_sources.actual_read_scope: Architecture II-C/transport layer PDFpp3–4, web298–369; keyword searches coupl/congestion. No full article review.
primary_nearest_sources.finding: Read/write transport is decoupled through configurable FIFOs and a dataflow element; the article discusses replacing a small FIFO with SRAM for full buffering. The exact first-R/AW policy is evidenced by the local primary source module, not inferred from an abstract or the failed keyword search.

primary_nearest_sources.title: iDMA official source repository
primary_nearest_sources.actual_read_scope: Local checked-in src/idma_channel_coupler.sv and its idma_backend call; remote repository search result only, no assertion that current master equals the local revision.
primary_nearest_sources.finding: Existing first-return write coupling is a real implementable baseline. Combined ordinary control above is an explicit architectural construction, not falsely labeled a published implementation.

stop_decision: Keep the paired return-envelope contract as a positive architecture candidate; do not send these two scenes to RTL as an innovation test, since the complete ordinary control predicts the same outcomes. The only remaining question from this card is a bounded complete-state/interface-cost comparison or a genuinely different capability; no further fixture repair is authorized by this card.
